long_biography.plain_text:
Mikati entered government as public works and transport minister, then represented Tripoli in parliament. Chosen to lead a transitional cabinet in 2005, he declined to contest the election that administration supervised, emphasizing institutional neutrality. Later appointments returned him to national leadership for two additional periods.

Outside government, he founded forums promoting centrist dialogue and participated in international policy organizations. Alongside his family, he oversees the Azm and Saade Association and the Mikati Foundation, whose work spans social development, education, medicine and charitable programs in Lebanon and other developing regions. His academic links include degrees from the American University of Beirut and executive study at INSEAD and Harvard.
